title: KV cache compaction improvements (epic): reduce fragmentation + burst tail latency
creator: Talia Benson
body:
Context
Today our KV arena behavior under mixed sequence lengths + churn can leave long-lived allocations interleaved with short-lived blocks, driving fragmentation and occasionally forcing expensive allocator/defrag work on the hot path. Under burst load this shows up as p95/p99 spikes (and in worst cases opportunistic evictions at bad times or OOM/request shedding). This epic tracks the end-to-end delivery of KV cache compaction + a safe, tier-aware eviction strategy integrated with the scheduler, plus the metrics/guardrails needed to roll it out.

Goals (what success looks like)
- Reduce KV allocator fragmentation in sustained decode workloads without harming steady-state throughput.
- Decrease burst tail latency (p95/p99) in mixed-length + churn scenarios.
- Introduce an eviction strategy that is correctness-safe, tier/model aware, and observable.
- Provide operational guardrails: budget limits, backpressure integration, and kill-switches.
- Ship in runtime-1.22 behind a feature flag with staged rollout: internal canary -> hosted subset -> dedicated pools.

Non-goals (initial release)
- No customer-facing UI in Console; config is via runtime flags/rollout tooling only.
- No major kernel rewrites beyond minimal copy/pack primitives needed for relocation.

Primary owners / working group
- Exec sponsor: Mateo Alvarez
- Tech lead: Omar El-Sayed
- Allocator/compaction: Samir Qureshi
- Scheduler integration: Sofia Ivanova (with Julian Moore for instrumentation)
- Correctness review: Noah Patel
- Observability standards + dashboards: Allison Grant (with Logan Wright / Caleb Johnson for ingestion)
- SRE rollout + SLO guardrails: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes
- Perf harness + tests: Marcus Reed / Rina Kobayashi / Sahana Iyer
- Feature flag + rollout plumbing: Benji Okafor

Milestones
1) Measurement + KPIs locked (Done)
- Repro fragmentation + tail spikes with benchmark-lab generator and perf-canary mixed-length burst scenario.
- Agree on KPIs: fragmentation ratio, bytes moved, compaction time, eviction rate, and latency correlation.

2) Observability foundation (In progress)
- Implement allocator-level fragmentation/health metrics and standardize names per perf standards.
- Dashboards panels + exemplar traces (compaction spans) wired to hosted + canary clusters.

3) Core compaction mechanism (Planned -> In progress)
- Incremental/budgeted compaction worker with safe stop conditions.
- Relocation primitives + allocator free-list changes behind feature flag.

4) Scheduler budgeting + backpressure integration (Planned)
- Enforce compaction budget at scheduling boundaries (prefill/decode transition) to avoid decode stalls.
- Integrate with overload/backpressure so we don’t ‘fight’ burst traffic (e.g., compaction pauses under high queue depth).

5) Tier-aware eviction policy (Planned)
- Tier-aware LRU by sequence with pinned session handling.
- Explicit interaction with prefix-cache/preemptible cached prefixes (evict preemptible first).

6) Correctness + stress tests (Planned)
- Long-lived sessions + high churn + cancellations during relocation.
- Validate no token correctness regressions, no leaks, and bounded stalls.

7) Rollout readiness (Planned)
- Kill-switch and config propagation verified.
- Runbook + known risks published.
- Canary gating criteria met for hosted, then expand to dedicated pools.

Rollout plan (staged)
- Stage 0 (internal): runtime team canary clusters only; flag off by default; metrics/dashboards validated.
- Stage 1 (hosted subset): enable for a small cohort of hosted traffic with strict rollback triggers; daily review.
- Stage 2 (hosted broader): expand by region/model profile if stable.
- Stage 3 (dedicated): enable per-pool with customer success coordination and opt-out path.

Rollout gating criteria (must-haves)
- Correctness: no correctness test failures; no increase in cancellation-related errors; allocator invariants hold under stress.
- Performance: no throughput regression >1% in steady-state decode; no p99 latency regression >3% vs control in canary. (Any regression must have a root cause + mitigation before expansion.)
- Fragmentation: sustained fragmentation ratio reduced meaningfully in mixed-length burst scenario (target: >=25% reduction vs baseline at steady state; exact threshold tracked per-model in benchmark sheet).
- Compaction overhead: compaction time on the hot path must remain within budget (budgeted per scheduler cycle); bytes moved is bounded and does not trend unbounded under churn.
- Eviction safety: eviction does not break pinned sessions; eviction counters correlate with configured tier policies; no spikes in ‘forced evictions’ during bursts.
- Ops: kill-switch verified end-to-end (config propagation latency understood and documented); oncall runbook validated by SRE; alerts tuned to avoid false positives.

Current status / notes
- We have reproduced the problem reliably with mixed-length + churn workload generator and have early evidence that allocator free-list changes + compaction reduce fragmentation, but scheduler integration is required to avoid occasional decode stalls during relocation.
- SRE requested explicit rollback conditions tied to both p99 and compaction bytes moved (to catch pathological compaction loops).
- We had one canary spike correlated with compaction tracing overhead; tracing is being made cheaper and/or sampled.

Implementation sequencing (preferred)
1) ENG-4822 metrics first (unblocks dashboards + gating)
2) ENG-4826 kill-switch/config plumbing (unblocks safe canary)
3) ENG-4823 allocator + compaction core
4) ENG-4824 scheduler hook for budgeting
5) ENG-4825 eviction policy
6) ENG-4827 stress tests
7) ENG-4828 perf canary scenario + thresholds
8) ENG-4830 dashboard panels polish
9) ENG-4829 release plan + comms

Risks / open questions
- How aggressive can compaction be before it causes measurable decode jitter? (Mitigation: strict budgeting in scheduler + pause under backpressure.)
- Relocation under cancellation: ensure we don’t leak pages or leave sequences in partial state. (Mitigation: stress tests + explicit cancellation handling path.)
- Interaction with prefix caching: ensure eviction prioritizes preemptible cached prefixes rather than active sequences. (Mitigation: tier-aware policy + counters.)

Decision log (high level)
- Compaction will be budgeted by bytes moved/time per scheduler phase; background compaction is allowed only when queue depth is low and is always preemptible.
- Eviction policy will be tier-aware LRU with pinned sessions; eviction is a last resort after compaction attempts when fragmentation/pressure exceeds thresholds.

Comms
- Weekly update in #eng-runtime and a short note to SRE + Release Train when canary expands.
- PM stakeholders (Hosted + Dedicated) will get a one-pager of expected customer-facing impact once defaults are finalized.

Exit criteria for closing epic
- Feature shipped in runtime-1.22 with staged rollout completed (hosted + at least one dedicated cohort).
- Metrics + dashboards meet standard, alerts tuned, and runbook is adopted by oncall.
- Bench suite includes fragmentation scenario; regression thresholds enforced in CI/perf-canary.
comments: 2026-01-11 (Omar El-Sayed): Kicked off epic. Goal is to land metrics + kill-switch first so we can iterate safely. Samir + Sofia aligned on incremental compaction with scheduler budgeting; background compaction only when queue depth is low.

2026-01-18 (Sean Gallagher): SRE needs explicit rollback triggers that don’t wait for customer tickets. Proposal: rollback if p99 > baseline +3% for 10m AND compaction_bytes_moved/s > threshold OR eviction_rate spikes. Also need a confirmed kill-switch propagation time for hosted clusters.

2026-01-27 (Allison Grant): Metric naming should follow the kv-cache fragmentation metrics standard. Please avoid per-model high-cardinality labels in the hot path; use model_profile and tier only. Add tracing exemplars for relocation steps to correlate with latency spikes.

2026-02-06 (Sofia Ivanova): Scheduler hook proposal: enforce compaction budget at decode boundary; if we’re in a sustained decode loop and queue depth is elevated, skip compaction step entirely (backpressure integration). Needs a small amount of instrumentation to avoid regressions.

2026-02-14 (Rafael Mendes): Oncall needs a simple decision tree: if p99 + compaction spikes, flip kill-switch; if OOM risk, reduce compaction threshold / enable eviction for low-priority tier. Runbook draft is in progress; please include ‘how to confirm compaction is disabled’ checks.

2026-02-20 (Samir Qureshi): Found an edge case with cancelled requests during relocation; fixed in follow-up PR and added a stress test harness case. Remaining work is tying budgeting into scheduler to prevent occasional 5-15ms hiccups under burst.
